ce_bugs.text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Persisting guests before calendar and email delivery makes a downstream failure unrecoverable by retry because the uniqueness filter rejects those already-saved guests.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — A guest addition submitted after cancellation still mutates the booking and can send CONFIRMED invitations because the handler never checks booking status.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — Attendee-initiated additions use the attendee’s credentials instead of the organizer’s credentials to update the organizer’s calendar event.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — A calendar-update exception leaves guests committed without invitations and the same retry is rejected because those guests already exist.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The unbounded guests array lets one mutation create arbitrarily many attendees and materialize matching calendar and notification work, exhausting request resources.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — A calendar-provider failure occurs after attendees are committed, leaving the booking unsynced and making client retries fail because the guests already exist.

mrv_findings.text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — [P1 confidence 75] `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` initializes the calendar updater with the requesting attendee's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, so an explicitly allowed attendee cannot reliably update the organizer's external calendar.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — [P1 confidence 100] `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` runs after attendee insertion has committed, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted without invitations and a retry is rejected by the existing-attendee filter before it can repair synchronization.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:94 — [P1 confidence 100] `id: bookingId,` is the only write predicate and no booking-status check precedes it, allowing cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings to acquire guests and emit the new templates' unconditional CONFIRMED calendar invitations.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — [P2 confidence 100] `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(` only removes addresses already stored and never deduplicates the input array accepted by the server schema, so repeated new addresses reach createMany and either create duplicate attendees or fail the entire request under a uniqueness constraint.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — [P2 confidence 100] `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` passes an event without any team property, making the email manager's team-member notification branch unreachable for this endpoint and omitting collective hosts from organizer notifications.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — [P1 confidence 100] `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails");` discards delivery failures and then returns success without a retry record, leaving newly persisted guests permanently uninformed because resubmitting the same addresses is rejected as already present.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:56 — [P3 confidence 100] `setIsInvalidEmail(true);` has no corresponding reset on editing, successful validation, success, or `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, so an invalid submission leaves the error visible after correction and subsequent reopening unless the user explicitly clicks Cancel.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — [P2 confidence 100] `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares an unnormalized guest against lowercase blacklist entries, allowing a caller to bypass the configured block with an uppercase domain such as blocked@EXAMPLE.COM and send the invitation to the same mailbox.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P2 confidence 75] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` accepts arbitrarily many copies of a previously absent address, which the handler inserts individually and the email manager sends individually, allowing an authorized attendee to amplify one request into repeated invitations to a victim mailbox despite the client-only uniqueness check.
